senses.gloss: (b. h.; interch. with שָׁחַח)to curve; to bend, bow; to lower one’s self.
units: <cite ref="Tosefta Berakhot 1:9">Tosef. Ber. I, 9</cite>; <cite ref="Berakhot 34a:14">Ber. 34ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 39">Gen. R. s. 39</cite>, a. e., v. <cite ref="U00634"><he>שָׁחַח</he></cite>. Pesik. Shek., p. 11ᵇ (ref. to <cite ref="Isaiah 2:9">Is. II, 9</cite>) <he>יודע אני ששָׁחוּ … והָשְׁפַּלְתִּי אני והם</he> I know that Israel lowered themselves by bowing to the calf, and I and they were humbled; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 386">Yalk. Ex. 386</cite>; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 260">Yalk. Is. 260</cite>; Tanḥ. Ki Thissa 4; <cite ref="Pesikta Rabbati 10:1">Pesik. R. s. 10</cite> <he>אימתי שחו ונשפלו</he> when was it that they bent and were lowered?; a. fr.

<cite ref="Mishnah Sanhedrin 7:6">Snh. VII, 6</cite> (<cite ref="Sanhedrin 60b">60ᵇ</cite>) <cite ref="U00640"><he>המִשְׁתַּחֲוֶה</he></cite> he that prostrates himself (before an idol). Ib. 62ᵃ <he>זיבח … וה׳ וכ׳</he> if a person sacrificed, burnt incense, offered libation, and prostrated himself, all in one act.

<cite ref="Yoma 69a">Yoma 69ᵃ</cite> <he>כיון שראה … וה׳ לפניו</he> when he (king Alexander) saw Simon the righteous, he alighted from his chariot and threw himself down before him; <he>מלך … יִשְׁתַּחֲוֶה וכ׳</he> should a great king like thee prostrate himself before this Jew?; a. fr.
